report.headline: Usage projected to grow modestly above EuroLeague average; shooting projection carries no real information

projection.text: Projected usage rate rises to 22.8% in the EuroLeague, up from an NBA usage rate of 18.3%, and sits above the EuroLeague average of 20.3%.

risks.text: The true shooting projection model is worse than the trivial league-mean baseline (4.7% error for both), so the 56.6% true shooting figure should not be treated as informative despite being cited.
In the source season this player's usage (-0.34 sd) and true shooting (-0.37 sd) both sat below the NBA average, meaning the projected EuroLeague gains rest on a below-average NBA baseline.

Players who actually make this NBA-to-EuroLeague move already sit only 0.31 standard deviations above their own league's average, so the projection describes a modestly-selected mover rather than an NBA standout.
Two full seasons elapsed between the last recorded NBA season and the EuroLeague move, a gap not reflected in the usage or shooting projections themselves.

strengths.text: The usage projection model outperforms the best trivial baseline (3.3% mean absolute error versus 4.3%), so the usage estimate is a genuine signal rather than noise.

The fitted slope for usage on this transition path is 0.986, meaning nearly all of a player's standing relative to their source league carries across, supporting the projected rise above the EuroLeague average.
Projected true shooting of 56.6% would land essentially at the EuroLeague average of 56.1%, consistent with a full offensive role rather than a diminished one.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage runs from 18.7% to 27.0%, an 8.3-point span against a EuroLeague usage standard deviation of only 4.2% — enough to rank this player but not to pin down an exact role, and the 95% interval widens further to 16.5%-29.2%.
